title: Shape, texture and pattern — Image Wiki

rules.rule: If a repeated element is regular enough that you can predict it, the whole area collapses into a single field known as a pattern.
rules.evidence: A pattern is repetition regular enough that you can predict it. Once you can predict it, you stop examining it, and the whole area collapses into a single field.

rules.rule: If an object's outline merges with its surroundings when squinting, it loses its shape identity and becomes part of a texture or background.
rules.evidence: Check the subject against the background as a silhouette. Is its outline still separable, or does it merge? If it merges, see Gestalt grouping.

rules.rule: If light is frontal, texture disappears; if raking (parallel to surface), every bump casts a shadow revealing texture.
rules.evidence: Raking light reveals texture; frontal light kills it. Put the source almost parallel to the surface and every bump gets a long shadow; put it behind the camera and the shadows hide behind the bumps that cast them.
